text:
AnitaP: Thanks again for joining the all-hands. Leaving this thread open for follow-up Qs specifically about hiring, team sizing, and internal mobility. Drop anything we didn't get to.

MattG: Quick one — for infra we heard 'more hiring next quarter' — can you confirm rough headcount targets by team (infra/runtime/platform) so managers can plan interviews?

AnitaP: Good call. Short answer: we approved a 30 FTE increase for FY27 across eng/product/support, with ~60% earmarked for infra/runtime and platform (so ~18 seats). The rest are split between product (6) and support/customer-facing roles (6). These are high level and still flexible based on early Q allocations. :bar_chart:

Leo: To add — infra/runtime stretch will prioritize latency/cost work (batching, kernel improvements) and Dedicated ops. We'll publish a team-level breakdown next Tue, but managers should assume interviews start mid-next-quarter.

SarahP: On product side, the 6 seats include 2 PMs focused on rollout/observability, 2 UX/Product engineers for Console, and 2 for Optimize features. We're trying to keep hiring scoped to clear PMFs so we don't overhire early.

JamalR: Recruiting note: we'll create reqs for infra/runtime first. If you're an EM or IC planning rotations, please ping me with a 1-paragraph "why move" and your manager's OK. Internal moves get priority in scheduling. Link to internal mobility form: https://redwood/intern-mobility (internal-only).

MattG: Thanks Jamal — will share with my team. Any changes to interview loop for infra roles?

Leo: Interview loop: one system-design-ish exercise (30–45m), a coding/optimization deep dive (45m), and a culture + collaboration chat (30m). We also want a short take-home micro-benchmark for senior infra folks (optional but helpful). Expect some emphasis on SLO-driven engineering and telemetry.

XenaF: Quick fiscal note: budget is committed but phased — hires will be greenlit in two tranches (Q1 and Q3 of FY27) contingent on revenue targets. If revenue lags, we may push some roles to later in the year. We do intend to keep the infra hires front-loaded for product continuity.

AnitaP: On org changes — we aren't doing a full-scale reorg right now. We're adjusting spans for some infra teams: two small teams will merge under Runtime lead to reduce coordination costs. Affected folks will get notified by managers this week. This is not a headcount reduction, just re-scope.

MattG: Can you clarify manager promotion timing vs. team moves? If someone takes a new manager role as part of this merge, when does compensation/promotion happen?

AnitaP: Good question. If a role change includes a promotion, compensation adjustments are effective at the time of the formal offer/approval (usually within 30 days of the move). We're trying to avoid delayed promotions — talk to People and Finance early.

SarahP: For PMs/ICs who are worried about role scope changing — we will publish updated role docs and success metrics. If you want to opt into a different charter, talk to your director; we'll try to support shadowing and a 60-day trial.

JamalR: Also — a reminder for hiring managers: prioritize internal candidates first (per policy). If you plan to interview externally, let recruiting know and mark the req as "open to internal" so we can route matches.

MattG: One last ask — can leadership share a short checklist for managers to communicate to teams when structural changes are announced? Keeps messaging consistent.

AnitaP: Yes — we'll publish a one-pager: 1) why the change, 2) what stays same, 3) timeline, 4) people impacted and next steps, 5) who to contact. Expect that in #devex and the all-hands follow-up doc by EOD Friday.

AllHandsBot: Reminder: recording and slides from today's all-hands are at https://redwood/all-hands/2472964821.

Leo: Thanks all. If there are private concerns about role changes or compensation, DM People or me directly. Appreciate the patience while we scale. :handshake:
